statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42013: an oversized Subject Alternative Name made GnuTLS certificate validation fall back to checking the Common Name, which could let a remote attacker bypass proper hostname validation. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-8 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1849) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/29801bef00ecc0f23c0bac4cd333b269cd2c1af4. Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42013), which applies the 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version; the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 records this CVE, and its libgnutls.so.30 library on both architectures contains the debug messages the fix adds ("oversized SAN ignored, disabling CN fallback" and "oversized SAN ignored, disabling DN fallback"). The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources sort below it and are reported as affected.
